body:
What is PAHAL?

PAHAL stands for Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh. It is also known as the Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG (DBTL) programme.

PAHAL changes how an applicable LPG subsidy reaches a consumer. Rather than functioning as a programme for issuing a new LPG connection, it provides a mechanism for transferring the subsidy directly to an eligible consumer's bank account.

The programme is administered under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, with oil marketing companies involved in identifying eligible LPG consumers and processing the relevant arrangements.

When was PAHAL introduced?

The modified DBTL programme called PAHAL was relaunched in 54 districts on 15 November 2014 and extended to the rest of the country on 1 January 2015.

For chronology-based questions, both dates are meaningful: 2014 identifies the initial modified rollout, while 1 January 2015 identifies nationwide extension.

How does the direct-benefit mechanism work?

Under the basic PAHAL arrangement, an LPG consumer who is eligible for a government subsidy obtains an LPG refill through the applicable distributor arrangement. The subsidy due to that consumer is then transferred into the consumer's registered bank account.

The essential point is the separation between purchasing an LPG refill and receiving an applicable subsidy through a bank transfer. The amount transferred depends on the prevailing entitlement and relevant government conditions.

The modified scheme initially allowed consumers to become eligible for the transfer process through arrangements involving either Aadhaar-linked details or direct linking of the relevant bank account with the LPG consumer identity. Current authentication and booking requirements must be distinguished from these historical launch arrangements.

Difference between PAHAL and PM Ujjwala

FeaturePM UjjwalaPAHAL
Primary purposeProvide eligible poor households with an LPG connectionTransfer applicable LPG subsidy to an eligible consumer
Main beneficiary conditionEligible adult woman from a poor household without an existing household connectionLPG consumer who satisfies the applicable subsidy conditions
Nature of benefitConnection equipment and specified initial benefitsApplicable subsidy deposited in a bank account
Nationwide rolloutLaunched in 2016Extended nationwide in 2015

A PMUY beneficiary may also receive an applicable refill subsidy through the direct-benefit mechanism. However, PAHAL is not restricted by definition to women receiving Ujjwala connections. The programmes concern different aspects of the LPG system.

Current status

PAHAL remained an operating LPG subsidy-delivery framework at the 16 November 2026 cutoff. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas continued to list PAHAL among its programmes and initiatives in its website information updated in October 2026.

Its continuing operation does not imply that every LPG consumer receives an equal subsidy. An eligible transfer requires a subsidy entitlement under the applicable policy.

Prelims focus

  • PAHAL: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh; also called DBTL.
  • Initial modified rollout: 15 November 2014 in 54 districts.
  • Nationwide extension: 1 January 2015.
  • Nodal ministry: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
  • Main purpose: transfer an eligible LPG consumer's applicable subsidy to a bank account.
  • Trap: PAHAL is a subsidy-transfer mechanism, not a scheme that itself grants a new LPG connection.

[Sources: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, 'Launch of PAHAL (DBTL) Scheme on 1st January 2015 in Entire Country', PIB, 31 December 2014; Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, 'Pahal Scheme for LPG', PIB, 11 March 2015; Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, official website, 'Marketing – PAHAL', section 'PAHAL/DBTL', last updated 6 October 2026; consulted 16 November 2026.]

title: PAHAL: Direct Transfer of LPG Subsidy to Eligible Consumers

body:
Identify a scheme through its principal benefit

A reliable way to distinguish these energy programmes is to identify what the beneficiary receives, which authority administers the scheme and whether the programme remains open or has concluded.

Similar-sounding names are not enough. In particular, a programme containing the word solar may concern a residential rooftop, an agricultural pump, a solar power plant or the electricity supplied through an agricultural feeder.

Scheme-to-purpose and status comparison

SchemeAuthorityPrincipal beneficiary or benefitStatus on 16 November 2026
DDUGJYUnion Ministry of PowerRural network strengthening, feeder separation and village electrificationClosed on 31 March 2022
SaubhagyaUnion Ministry of PowerElectricity connections for willing unelectrified rural and eligible urban householdsClosed on 31 March 2022
PM Surya GharUnion MNRECentral assistance for qualifying residential rooftop solar installationsActive
PM-KUSUMUnion MNRE; State implementing agenciesAgricultural solar generation, standalone pumps and solarisationPublished period ended 31 March 2026; eligible sanctioned work has specified extensions
Kisan SuryodayGovernment of GujaratDaytime electricity supply for agricultural consumersState initiative under implementation
PM UjjwalaUnion Ministry of Petroleum and Natural GasDeposit-free LPG connections for eligible women from poor householdsActive
PAHALUnion Ministry of Petroleum and Natural GasBank transfer of applicable LPG subsidyOperating subsidy-delivery framework

Understand the chronological development

The programmes were introduced at different stages and for different purposes. DDUGJY began strengthening rural electricity infrastructure in 2014, while Saubhagya was launched in 2017 to connect remaining willing households. PM-KUSUM followed in 2019 to support agricultural solarisation, and Gujarat launched Kisan Suryoday in 2020 to provide daytime agricultural electricity.

For cooking fuel, the modified PAHAL subsidy-transfer arrangement was rolled out nationally by January 2015, before PM Ujjwala was launched in May 2016. For residential rooftop solar, PM Surya Ghar was introduced in February 2024.

Important scheme-pair distinctions

DDUGJY and Saubhagya

DDUGJY's main emphasis was the rural distribution network and village electrification. Saubhagya's main emphasis was the connection of remaining willing households. Both programmes are now closed, although later schemes continue related work.

PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM

PM Surya Ghar primarily supports residential rooftop solar. PM-KUSUM primarily supports agricultural solar applications, including standalone pumps, solarisation of grid-connected agricultural supply and decentralised plants. Their beneficiaries and financial-assistance arrangements are not interchangeable.

PM-KUSUM and Gujarat Kisan Suryoday

PM-KUSUM is a Union renewable-energy programme implemented with States. Kisan Suryoday is a Gujarat Government electricity-supply initiative. Daytime power supplied to a farmer does not establish that the farmer has received a subsidised personal solar pump.

PM Ujjwala and PAHAL

PM Ujjwala helps an eligible poor household obtain an LPG connection. PAHAL helps deliver an applicable LPG subsidy to a consumer's bank account. The connection benefit and the subsidy-transfer mechanism can operate together, but they have different eligibility and administrative purposes.

Remember how to interpret dated facts

When a question mentions the closure of an electrification programme, it is important to distinguish the completion of that scheme from the continuation of the government's broader work in the same sector. DDUGJY and Saubhagya closed in 2022, while RDSS remained an ongoing distribution-sector programme in 2026.

Similarly, PM-KUSUM's published period ended in March 2026, but MNRE subsequently allowed particular sanctioned projects to continue under defined conditions. A dated extension is not the same thing as an unrestricted new application period.

Finally, LPG subsidy amounts and refill limits should always be connected to the relevant decision date or financial year. A figure approved for FY 2025–26 need not remain the applicable figure under a later announcement.

Prelims focus

  • Ministry of Power: DDUGJY and Saubhagya.
  • MNRE: PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM.
  • Government of Gujarat: Kisan Suryoday.
  • Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas: PM Ujjwala and PAHAL.
  • Closed schemes: DDUGJY and Saubhagya, both closed on 31 March 2022.
  • Trap: A scheme's announced target, its historical achievement and its current operating status are 3 different facts.

[Sources: Ministry of Power, 'Electrification of Villages', PIB Release 2226925, 12 February 2026; MNRE, 'PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana', Cabinet approval, PIB Release 2010133, 29 February 2024; MNRE, official PM-KUSUM scheme description and Office Memorandum dated 28 September 2026; Prime Minister's Office, Gujarat Kisan Suryoday launch announcement, PIB Release 1666803, 22 October 2020; Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, official PMUY portal, 'About PMUY'; Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, official website, 'Marketing – PAHAL'; consulted 16 November 2026.]
